title: 1 · The memory

title: 2 · Now

title: 4 · The idea
text: So I picked up my old Game Boy again, and while playing with it, it hit me. It's the most honest screen I ever owned. It only does what my thumbs tell it to do. What if it guarded my keys? That's where I came up with kagiboy: a cartridge for the Game Boy you already have.

title: 5 · How it feels
text: Turning it on feels like a new save file of a game. You mash the buttons and shake the Game Boy, which creates the randomness needed for your seed. The cartridge reads every request itself and puts the amount and the address on the tiny screen. Nothing moves until you hold A.

title: 6 · Try it
text: You don't have to take my word for it. Open our website right now and test it out for yourself. Currently you are able to do devnet transactions on six different networks, and we also have in-app swaps, which are powered by the SODAX SDK.

title: 8 · Who it's for
text: I'm making this for people like me, kids who grew up with a Game Boy and somehow ended up in crypto. You put it on your shelf, next to your computer, or give it to someone you love. We're starting with the cartridge, numbered colourways, a mystery edition only for Japan, and a bundle with a restored Game Boy.

title: 9 · Close
text: What comes next is that we want to go from a browser emulation to a real cartridge. And alongside this, we want to do multiple security audits before anyone can buy one. Crypto shouldn't feel like something you are scared of. It should feel like that one day at the flea market, where you got your first Game Boy.
